headline: Learning Opportunities Fund reopened for students affected by strike action
detail: Grants of up to £500 for students whose learning was disrupted by the industrial action of 24 February to 20 March 2020.
quote: The Learning Opportunities Fund has reopened for applications from students whose learning was affected by the strike action that took place between 24 February and 20 March 2020.
notes: A pre-pandemic disruption being settled during the pandemic. The strike ended four days before the national lockdown.

headline: Biosafety guidance approved for work with coronavirus samples
detail: Covering research using samples from confirmed or suspected patients and work with the virus directly.
quote: The UCL Genetic Modification & Biosafety Committee has approved new guidance for those planning to work with samples from confirmed or suspected coronavirus patients, or those planning to work with the virus directly.

headline: UCL Together has supplied 497 days of redeployed support in four weeks
quote: To date, we have provided 497 days of additional support to teams across the university by matching volunteers to those departments who have requested help.
notes: A measured outcome for the scheme launched on 27 March, which is rare in the record; most initiatives are announced and never quantified.

headline: Recruitment freeze and capital spending paused as income falls
detail: With drastic cuts to non-pay expenditure to build cash reserves, and additional borrowing drawn down.
quote: We have, of course, taken immediate action to cut costs: introducing a recruitment freeze (so we prioritise those who are already part of our community); pausing or cancelling significant elements of capital expenditure
notes: The pivot from crisis response to financial survival, one month into lockdown.

headline: Provost takes a 20% pay reduction donated to the student hardship fund
detail: For six months from 1 August 2020, alongside a Give as You Earn scheme opened for the Senior Management Team.
quote: I have volunteered to take a pay reduction of 20% of my salary, which will be donated to the student hardship fund, for six months from August 1st.
notes: Filed on the effective date of 1 August 2020; announced 24 April in issue 31.

headline: UCL declines an across-the-board pay freeze adopted by other universities
quote: You may be aware that other universities have announced an across-the-board pay freeze. This is something that we are not yet considering and we will exhaust all other options before we do so.
notes: A rare explicit contrast with sector practice, and one the sector track should be able to test once the comparator institutions are identified in stage 2.

headline: Single-year budgeting adopted with the contribution model set aside
detail: Normal processes suspended through Term 1, pending clarity on tuition fee income.
quote: We will do single-year budgeting, in which we set temporarily aside our usual processes through Term 1.

headline: Looking out for our students phone campaign launched
detail: Staff volunteers calling students to check how they were coping, committing at least one day a week to the end of May.
quote: Colleagues from across UCL have launched ‘Looking out for our students’, a new phone call campaign to keep in touch with our students and help them feel cared for during the coronavirus outbreak.

headline: Building closures to be reviewed on 8 May, with 15 May the earliest reopening
detail: Explicitly contingent on whether the national lockdown was extended again.
quote: We will review our building closures and remote working policy again on Friday 8 May, and the earliest date that we could start reopening our buildings would be Friday 15 May.
notes: The second review date to pass without reopening, after 1 May. Campus did not reopen to most staff in 2020 at all.

headline: Grant-funded staff offered furlough with UCL topping pay up to 100%
detail: Staff due to leave in May or June had leaving dates extended to the end of June; those due to leave in July or August were extended to the end of August on core funding.
quote: We will offer those grant-funded staff who were expecting to depart UCL during May and June 2020 the opportunity to be furloughed, and have their leaving date extended until the end of June.
notes: UCL's use of the national Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme. The newsletter notes the government share fell to about 60% in higher education because of pension arrangements, and that UCL made up the difference.

headline: Furloughed staff barred from any work, including writing up UCL results
quote: It is important to note that any staff on furlough cannot undertake any work for UCL. This means that activities such as writing up results obtained at UCL and analysing UCL data are not allowed.
notes: A condition of the national scheme with a sharp effect on research careers, and the clearest instance in the record of national policy constraining UCL rather than merely prompting it.

headline: Self-funded PhD students given until 31 July to pay final fee instalment
detail: Extended from 2 May, alongside Financial Assistance Fund grants of up to £3,000 prioritised for self-funders.
quote: the third and final instalment of tuition fees has now been extended from 2 May until 31 July 2020

headline: UCL-Ventura designs downloaded by over 1,800 teams in 105 countries
detail: Twenty-four days after the designs were released free of charge, with prototypes built in Mexico, South Africa, Canada, Bulgaria and Russia.
quote: In the 24 days since they were published, the designs have been downloaded by over 1,800 teams in 105 countries, representing non-profits, manufacturers, health experts and research institutes.

headline: Extenuating circumstances self-certified with no evidence required
detail: Introduced immediately before the summer assessment period began.
quote: changes have been made to UCL’s Extenuating Circumstances process, to reduce any burden on our students. Students can now self-certify and no longer need to provide evidence when applying.
notes: Extends the self-certification agreed on 20 March by removing the evidence requirement entirely.

headline: Provost asks staff to prioritise education over research for the crisis period
detail: With an assurance that the prioritisation would be recognised in appraisals and promotion cases.
quote: For this crisis period, I find myself needing to go further to ask you to prioritise education for the next few months, wherever and however you can.
notes: Justified in the same message by the dependence of research funding on overseas tuition fee income, which is the plainest statement in the record of why the teaching decisions mattered financially.

headline: Faculties told to decide which modules not to run in 2020-21
detail: Faculty Delivery Teams identifying modules best suited to online delivery rather than moving everything online.
quote: An excellent teaching programme for 2020-21 will necessarily be different from what we might have planned in more conventional times – and will require decisions about what not to run.

headline: Gold team has post-lockdown plans ready ahead of the government announcement
detail: Prepared in advance of the Prime Minister's expected statement on easing restrictions.
quote: UCL’s Gold team has developed plans for post-lockdown operations and an action plan has been considered over the last couple of weeks, which will be updated as soon as there is any Government announcement.
notes: Evidence of UCL preparing before rather than after a national announcement, which is what the lag analysis is meant to distinguish. The response itself came on 11 May, one day after the announcement of 10 May.

headline: Staff asked not to return to campus despite the easing of restrictions
detail: UCL's response to the Prime Minister's announcement of 10 May 2020, published the following day.
quote: We are asking everyone not to return to UCL for the time being, unless you are one of our key staff who have been on-site throughout the lockdown period.
notes: A one-day lag, and the substance is divergence rather than compliance: national restrictions eased and UCL did not. The counterpart to 13 March, where UCL moved first in the other direction.

headline: Phased return to begin with a small number of pilots, most likely in June
detail: Aimed at laboratory and research work that could not be done from home, with nobody compelled to take part.
quote: The first stage of reopening will comprise a small number of pilots, where we will consult with colleagues in specific areas to identify opportunities to start working on campus again, most likely in June.

headline: Reopening made explicitly conditional on the national reproduction number
quote: If the rate of infection (R) rises again nationally, then we acknowledge that we may have to row back on this cautious reopening plan.
notes: The clearest statement in the record that UCL's campus policy was indexed to a national epidemiological measure rather than to its own case counts, which did not yet exist. Directly relevant to the blog post's claim that the on-campus line tracks policy.

headline: No member of staff to be compelled to return for the pilots
detail: Transport, caring responsibilities and health concerns all accepted as reasons to decline.
quote: Please be assured that no one will be compelled to return to UCL for the pilots.
